text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Namibia's main opposition Democratic Turnhalle Alliance party has intensified its criticism of the Local Authorities Amendment Bill currently being debated in parliament. The bill provides for the next local elections in December to be held on the basis of a party list system instead of a ward system.
- The Cabinet has approved a Total Allowable Catch for deep sea fish species of 22,000 metric tonnes for 1997/98, comprising 12,000 mt for Orange Roughy and 10,000 mt for Alfonsio.

- The Cabinet has approved a national code on AIDS and employment based on constitutional principles, a corresponding code by the Southern African Development Community and existing labour legislation.
- McCarthy Retail Ltd, one of the largest retail groups in southern Africa, has listed on the Namibian Stock Exchange. The NSE's total market capitalisation is now close to N$150 billion.
